judges: Sanjay K. Agrawal C.A.V. Judgment J.
case_name: Smt. Milvanteen Bai And Another vs Devkibai And Another 5 Revp/53/2020

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Milvanteen Bai, Wd/o Late Gwal & Smt. Ramkumari Bai, Wd/o Rameshawar Yadav
parties.respondent_defendant: Devkibai, W/o Konda & State of Chhattisgarh, By Collector, Raipur

facts_of_case: The suit property was held by one Gwal Yadav. Plaintiff No.1 claims to be his first wife married in chudi form and plaintiff No.2 claims to be daughter out of the wedlock of Gwal with plaintiff No.1, whereas defendant No.1 claims that he is adopted daughter of Gwal.

legal_principles.principle: Children born to a married woman from an illicit relationship are not entitled to the benefit under Section 16 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
legal_principles.held: Gulab C. Gupta, J. speaking for the Madhya Pradesh High Court has clearly held that children born to married woman from illicit relationship are not entitled to the benefit under Section 16 of the Act.
cited_cases: Reshamlal Baswan vs. Balwant Singh Jwalasingh Punjabi and Others (1)
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to cases involving illegitimate children

legal_principles.principle: A marriage must be solemnised for the benefit under Section 16 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 to apply.
legal_principles.held: This provision has been interpreted to mean that there must be a marriage, which would be hit by the provisions of this Act and would not cover a relationship resulting from any other arrangement than the marriage.
cited_cases: M. Muthayya v. Kamu and Ors., AIR 1981 NOC 172
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to cases involving the application of Section 16

outcome.result: Appeal admitted for determination of substantial questions of law

use_for_drafting: advising on property division in matrimonial disputes
